newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COURT SUPPORTS C.BANK FPB INSOLVENCY CLAIM.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COURT SUPPORTS C.BANK FPB INSOLVENCY CLAIM.

text.p: Bulgaria's Supreme Court ruled in favour of a central bank appeal against a lower court's rejection of an insolvency claim against First Private Bank (FPB), a court official said.
"The Supreme Court overturned the ruling of the Sofia City Court, which rejected an insolvency suit filed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) against FPB," a court official told reporters.
"The Supreme Court returns the insolvency case against the FPB for reconsideration to the Sofia City Court and recommends to declare the bank insolvent," said the official.
FPB officials were not immediately available for comment.
The BNB put Bulgaria's biggest private bank, in receivership on May 17, 1996 and sought its insolvency through the Sofia City Court two weeks later.
The court rejected the BNB claim in December, saying it was not supported by enough evidence. The BNB appealed against that ruling to the Supreme Court.

The central bank retracted FPB's banking licence last month, citing its failure to collect loans and repay debts of over 200 billion levs to its major creditors during the one-year period of receivership.

Under a new Banking Law passed by parliament this week and due to come in force next week, courts can not rule against insolvency claims filed the BNB if the commercial bank's licence has been retracted.
The BNB has said that FPB owed over 100 billion levs to the state for repayments to depositors, and over 90 billion levs to the BNB at end-March.

The FPB had a heavily negative capital to risk assets ratio and its registered capital of two billion levs was not fully paid in, which prevented possibilities for attracting potential investors to increase the FPB capital, the BNB has said.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the IMF, Bulgarian banks should have a minimum six percent capital to risk assets ratio by the end of this year and eight percent by mid-1998 to comply with international standards. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
